detailed_rationale: [DATA] FY26 (ended Mar-2026): consolidated revenue Rs.33,653cr (+6.1% YoY), net profit Rs.3,503cr, EBITDA margin ~20.4%. Segment mix Q4FY26: US formulations 40% (Rs.3,543cr, -13% YoY on lower transient sales), Europe ~32% (Rs.2,795cr / EUR261mn, +30.2% YoY, Europe crossed EUR1bn for FY26 - a genuine milestone), APIs 14% (+25% QoQ), Growth Markets ~11% (+24.7% YoY to Rs.980cr), ARV ~4% (+6.4% YoY). Quarterly trend: Q2FY26 PAT Rs.848cr -> Q3FY26 Rs.910cr (+7.6% YoY, +7.3% QoQ, EBITDA-before-R&D margin 25.0%) -> Q4FY26 Rs.921cr (+2.0% YoY only) - sequential PAT growth is decelerating even as revenue holds up, consistent with press commentary flagging 'margin pressure clouds strong revenue growth' in Q4. Q1FY26 (year-ago base) PAT had fallen -10.2% YoY, so FY26 full-year growth is off a soft base. USFDA/plant status is the dominant fresh risk: Eugia Unit-III (Pashamylaram, Telangana) - a sterile-injectables/oncology site - was inspected 27-Jan to 6-Feb-2026 and classified OAI (Official Action Indicated) with 11 observations; Eugia is the vehicle for Aurobindo's stated USD1bn injectables-by-2026 goal and the complex-injectable/biosimilar launch pipeline underpinning the 'Aurobindo 2.0' margin-expansion thesis - remediation is guided 6-18 months, management expects FDA reinspection within ~8 months, and OAI-status facilities cannot get new ANDA approvals until cleared. Separately Unit-VII (Jedcherla) got a 9-observation Form-483 (Jan-Feb 2026) and Apitoria Pharma (API JV) got 3 observations (Dec-2025) - a pattern of findings across multiple sites, not a single isolated event, though Aurobindo's manufacturing base is large (25+ sites) so this is not single-plant-dependent existential risk the way it would be for a smaller name. [INFERENCE] Per this desk's base rate, OAI status historically escalates to a formal warning letter >75% of the time - this is a standing high-risk flag on the injectables growth leg specifically, not the whole franchise. Policy: US Section-232 pharma tariffs (100% on patented drugs/APIs, tiered rates effective 31-Jul-2026) explicitly EXCLUDE generics, biosimilars and their associated ingredients 'at this time' - Aurobindo is overwhelmingly a generics/API company so near-term direct tariff hit is low, but Commerce is required to advise within 1 year whether to extend scope to generics - that scope-creep clause is the actual risk, not the current carve-out. [DATA] Valuation: TTM P/E ~24-25x (share price ~Rs.1,544-1,547 in mid-to-late Jul-2026, market cap ~Rs.89,060cr) vs the stock's own 10-year median ~17.2x and the drug-manufacturers industry median ~21.2x - i.e. trading at a premium to both its own history and peers. Consensus 12-month target across ~28 analysts is ~Rs.1,519 (essentially flat-to-slightly-below the current price), though at least one bullish house (Nuvama) has a materially higher Rs.1,753 target on 16x FY28E EPS assuming the margin-expansion story plays out. Brokerage FY26-28E consensus: revenue CAGR ~15-17%, PAT CAGR ~24-26% (management separately guides FY27 EBITDA margin ~21%) - the PAT-CAGR outperformance over revenue-CAGR is entirely a bet on the Eugia/biosimilar margin-mix shift landing on schedule, which is precisely the leg now under an OAI cloud.
recommendation_rationale: No quant score exists yet for this name (first pass). On fundamentals alone: valuation is already rich vs both own history and peers with consensus target price roughly flat to current spot - little re-rating room is being offered for free even before the regulatory setback is digested. But the business itself is diversified (Europe now >EUR1bn and growing 30%, API and Growth Markets both recovering double-digit) and not single-plant dependent, so the Eugia OAI is a genuine but contained risk to ONE growth leg (complex injectables/biosimilars), not to the franchise. Net: priced for a smooth margin-expansion story that has just hit a credible regulatory obstacle - call it fully-priced-to-rich rather than a fresh Sell trigger. HOLD, not Sell.
